Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

whichever pronoun and adjective

also whichever of the two, whichever you like, either one

classical

Cic. Fam. 6.4.1: utercumque vīcerit

utercumque, utracumque, utrumcumque

relative pronoun and adjective

whichever (of two)

Rare, but classical (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • utervīs, utravīs, utrumvīs — whichever (of two) you like, either

    indefinite pronoun and adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 33: at minus habeō vīrium quam vestrum utervīs; Ter. Haut. 342: in aurem utramvīs ōtiōsē ut dormiās

    Either one, it does not matter which.

  • quīcumque, quaecumque, quodcumque — whichever (of several)

    relative pronoun and adjective · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.31.14: fortūnam, quaecumque accidat

    See “whatever”.

Examples

  • ita magnae utrimque cōpiae, ita parātae ad dēpugnandum esse dīcuntur, ut, utercumque vīcerit, nōn sit mīrum futūrum

    the forces on both sides are said to be so large and so ready to fight it out that, whichever of them wins, it will be no surpriseCic. Fam. 6.4.1

  • At minus habeō vīrium quam vestrum utervīs.

    But I have less strength than either of you.Cic. Sen. 33

  • in aurem utramvīs ōtiōsē ut dormiās

    so that you can sleep soundly on whichever ear you likeTer. Haut. 342

See also whatever, which.
